methodology: Bounded first-pass screening of the four final verses of Yunus (10:106–109) against Arabic and English Quran text (Pickthall and other translations). For 10:107, Hebrew Deuteronomy 32:39 and English translation consulted at Sefaria. No critical apparatus, manuscript witness or historical transmission route reviewed. No public verification.

ayat.summary: Prohibits invoking beings incapable of benefit or harm. Broad anti-idolatry motif; no distinctive earlier passage verified for this verse.
God alone removes harm and grants good; compare Deuteronomy 32:39 as a broad doctrinal motif, not an episode or proof of dependence.

candidates.translation: English rendering on Sefaria/Voices page consulted
candidates.similarity: Both deny that another power can override divine agency in adversity or rescue.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy's Song of Moses speaks in the divine first person of death, life, wounding and healing, and of no deliverer from God's hand; Qur'an 10:107 addresses the hearer and contrasts harm with bounty, forgiveness and mercy.
candidates.limits: Textual comparison at online Hebrew/English level only; critical edition, manuscript witnesses, compositional history and transmission route not checked. Broad theological resemblance, not demonstrated literary borrowing.

ayat.summary: Truth has come; guidance or error benefits or harms each person, while messenger is not a guardian over them. No precise prior passage verified.
Follow revelation, be patient until divine judgment. No passage-specific pre-Islamic source verified.

reconcile_before_merge: Yunus ends at 10:109; 10:110 does not exist. Check other open drafts and canonical main ledger before merge; PR #93 remains a verified-only RLS security gate.
